related_questions.question: What are the side effects of the 16 year old vaccine?

text_blocks.snippet: Common side effects for vaccines given at age 16 are generally mild and temporary, similar to those experienced by younger children. These typically include soreness, redness, or swelling at the injection site, as well as potential fever, headache, fatigue, muscle or joint pain, or feeling unwell. These reactions usually resolve within a few days. More serious reactions like severe allergic reactions are rare.
snippet_highlighted_words: soreness, redness, or swelling at the injection site, as well as potential fever, headache, fatigue, muscle or joint pain, or feeling unwell

list.snippet: Local Reactions: Soreness, redness, or swelling at the injection site are the most frequently reported side effects.
Systemic Reactions: Fever, headache, fatigue, muscle or joint pain, and feeling generally unwell can also occur.
Gastrointestinal: Nausea and diarrhea are also possible, though less common.
Fainting: Fainting after vaccination is a rare occurrence, but it can happen.
Severe Allergic Reactions (Anaphylaxis): While rare, severe allergic reactions can occur, but are typically handled by healthcare professionals.

list.title: High Fever:
list.snippet: If a high fever persists after taking over-the-counter pain relievers, it's best to consult with a doctor.

list.title: Severe Reactions:
list.snippet: If you experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction, such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face or throat, seek immediate medical attention.

list.title: Other Concerns:
list.snippet: If you have any concerns about your child's reaction to the vaccine, contact their healthcare provider.
